transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This symptom—tripping the kitchen power—is almost probably caused by an 'earth fault' inside the machine, where electricity is leaking to the metal casing. The most common cause in Indesit machines like yours is a failing heater element that has developed a short circuit; it often trips only when the water starts heating up. Less commonly, it could be the drain pump or internal wiring. Because this involves mains electricity and a safety hazard (the RCD tripping), please do not keep resetting the fuse box to use the machine. It is unsafe until fixed. To help identify which part might be failing: does the power trip happen immediately when you turn the dial on, or only once the machine starts heating the water (usually a few minutes into the cycle)?

Thanks, I'll keep notes on this. It only trips a few minutes into the wash, and only on the 40 or 60 degree ones. It has never tripped on cold washes, quick 30, or rinse and spin. I should say I have been resetting it each time so far, about 1 wash in 4 over the last month, but I haven't smelled any burning or seen any sparks.
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
Sorry, I got an error message instead of a reply. Did my last message come through? I've told you it only trips a few minutes into the 40 and 60 degree washes. What should I do next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Your notes confirm exactly what we suspected: because it only happens on hot washes, the fault is probably in the heating circuit. The most likely cause is the heater element itself developing an internal short to its metal casing (an earth fault), which trips your kitchen RCD as soon as it tries to heat up. Less commonly, the wiring insulation near the element terminals could be degrading. Because this involves a live electrical fault that can shock or start a fire if ignored, you must leave the machine unplugged and not use it again until a qualified engineer has replaced the faulty part (usually the heater element). Trying to bypass the trip is dangerous. Please arrange for an appliance engineer to inspect and repair it.

candidates: Drain pump or motor shorting to earth (medium)
Mains cable or internal wiring fault (low)
